name: Catholic Cross References
stage: seed — the marginal cross references of the original Douay-Rheims Bible, parsed
license: This dataset is public domain (see the repository LICENSE, the Unlicense). The seed data is CC0 1.0.

seed_source.what: The cross references printed in the margins of the original Douay-Rheims Bible — the New Testament at Rheims (1582) and the Old Testament at Douay (1609–1610).
seed_source.data: Transcribed as structured data by the Original Douay-Rheims project (thedouayrheims.com), released CC0 1.0 / public domain.

notes: Book names and numbering are the Douay-Rheims own (1–4 Kings, Paralipomenon, Esdras, Isaias, Jeremias, Ezechiel, Osee, Micheas, Sophonias, Aggeus, Zacharias, Malachias, Tobias, Ecclesiasticus, Machabees, Apocalypse; Psalms in Vulgate numbering).
A target with no verse (e.g. "Genesis 22") cites the whole chapter, as the margin printed it.
Targets in 3 Esdras, 4 Esdras, and the Prayer of Manasses — printed in the Douay Bible's appendix, not among the 73 books of the Catholic canon — carry "appendix_targets": true.
Every margin entry that could not be read as a definite reference is listed in dropped-entries.json with the reason. Nothing was guessed.
Reading conventions are documented in the README, under "How the margins were read".

Correction (v1.1.0, Nov 1, 2026): at 1 Peter 1:16 the raw margin reads "Lev. 11, 19. 20, 7." — Leviticus chapters 11 and 19, then chapter 20 verse 7 (all three carry the "be ye holy" words Peter quotes: 11:44-45, 19:2, 20:7). The v0.1.0 parse fused the chapter list into a single target "Leviticus 11:19" (an unclean-birds verse). Corrected to the chapter targets "Leviticus 11" and "Leviticus 19", the form this dataset already uses for chapter citations ("Deuteronomy 10", "Romans 2" in the same margin entry).
